subject: Staged patch proposal and emergency reversion plan for private deployment
messages:
From: ops@acmebank.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmebank.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster: proposed staged patch + emergency reversion plan

Maya —

Thanks for the earlier sync. Attached is our narrow-window proposal for the October patch run on the private VPC we host with Redwood. High level asks:

- We need clear version pinning for the control-plane and inference runtime (we're currently on rwinf v3.1).
- A documented maintenance window that minimises overlap with peak business hours (we prefer 01:00–05:00 local).
- A well-tested emergency reversion (fast rollback) path and owner for each step.
- Evidence that KV cache warm-up and prefix caching won't cause sustained latency spikes post-upgrade.

Attached: patch_manifest_v3.2.pdf (proposed binaries and checksums). Please confirm feasibility and provide a suggested canary schedule + abort criteria.

Thanks —
Ellen Cho
Lead Platform Ops, Acme Bank
On behalf of Acme Bank Private Cloud Team

[attachment: patch_manifest_v3.2.pdf]

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: ops@acmebank.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: proposed staged patch + emergency reversion plan

Ellen —

Thanks for the detailed proposal and the manifest. We can support the plan; next steps below and a couple of clarifying questions.

Planned approach (high level):
1) Canary phase: 1 control-plane node + 2 inference workers in a single AZ. Duration: 90 minutes of synthetic traffic + 60 minutes observation.
2) Staged rollout: slice by tag (pinset) — 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%, with 30-minute holds and automated health checks.
3) Fast rollback: if latency P95 > 2x baseline or error rate > 1.5% in any stage, immediate revert to pinned rwinf v3.1 image on that slice and pause rollout.

Questions:
- Can you confirm a 01:00–05:00 local maintenance window for the canary and initial slices?
- Are there regulatory audit windows we need to avoid (end-of-month batch jobs)?

I've copied Mina and Karthik for ops coordination and rollback ownership. Attached I'll send canary-runbook.md and netplan diffs for the proposed network changes.

Action items:
- Ellen: confirm maintenance window and any blackout windows (reply by EOD).
- Mina: can you own the rollback playbook and add the runbook checklist?
- Karthik: runbook review for network quiesce and BGP handling.

Thanks —
Maya Srinivasan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: canary-runbook.md]

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ops@acmebank.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: proposed staged patch + emergency reversion plan

Ellen / team —

I can own the rollback playbook. Drafting a compact checklist here for visibility; I'll attach a runnable play-by-play and test script by tomorrow morning. Key points:

Rollback owner and roles:
- Mina Haddad (Redwood): orchestrate rollback, run revert jobs, coordinate with Acme NetOps.
- Karthik Iyer (Redwood NetOps): perform network quiesce/unquiesce, validate routing and SR-IOV attachments.
- Soojin Lee (Redwood SRE): watch health metrics, flip traffic slices, validate cache integrity.

Critical rollback steps (short):
1) Abort rollout (automated trigger).
2) Revert slice images to rwinf v3.1 pinned image via artifact-relink (expected 7–12 min per slice).
3) Evict and drain faulty KV caches, then rehydrate from snapshot (estimated warm-up 10–15 min).
4) Run smoke inference suite and P95 latency check (3 test runs).
5) If reversion unsuccessful after two attempts, escalate to hotfix branch with controlled lateral rollback of control-plane nodes (owner: Mina).

Network changes: Karthik, I left a short diff in netplan-diff.txt referencing the VLAN mapping. Please confirm the BGP withdraw timeline to ensure minimal packet loss during slice cutover.

Attachments I'll provide: canary-runbook.md (detailed steps), netplan-diff.txt (network diff), and a verification checklist.

One more ask for Acme: please provide a single Slack contact or pager for emergency coordination during the window.

Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[attachment: netplan-diff.txt]

From: ops@acmebank.com

Maya / Mina —

Confirmed: 01:00–05:00 local (US/Eastern) maintenance window works for us for the canary and first two slices. No end-of-month batch jobs in that window. Our pager contact during the window will be #acmeops-oncall (Slack) and pager acct: +1-555-0132.

We reviewed the rollback checklist and the estimated times look acceptable; please proceed with finalizing the runbook and we will sign off on the preflight checklist by 2026-10-08 10:00 ET.
